**`code-block-header`** — Header bar above the code block.
- Background `{colors.surface-code}`, text `{colors.on-dark-muted}`, typography `{typography.caption}`, padding `{spacing.xs} {spacing.md}`, bottom border `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08)`.

### Documentation Components

**`feature-icon-tile`** — Cream-yellow feature icon callout.
- Background `{colors.cream}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.md}`, border `1px solid {colors.beige-deep}`.

**`industry-tile`** — Industry-vertical tile in solutions page grid.
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.xl}`, border `1px solid {colors.hairline-soft}`.

**`stat-cell`** — Stat-row cell ("75% more / 80% better").
- Background transparent, text `{colors.ink}`, typography `{typography.stat-display}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`.

**`customer-testimonial-card`** — Customer quote card (used inside Le Studio and Solutions pages).
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`, border `1px solid {colors.hairline-soft}`. Quote in `{typography.body-md}`, attribution in `{typography.body-sm}` `{colors.steel}`.

**`logo-wall-item`** — Customer logo wordmark cell.
- Background transparent, text `{colors.steel}`, typography `{typography.body-md-medium}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`.

**`faq-accordion-item`** — FAQ panel.
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xl}`, bottom border `1px solid {colors.hairline}`.

**`app-store-badge`** — App Store / Google Play download badge.
- Background `{colors.ink}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`, typography `{typography.caption-bold}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.sm} {spacing.md}`.

### Navigation

**Top Navigation (Marketing)** — Sticky white bar.
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, height ~64px, bottom border `1px solid {colors.hairline-soft}`.
- Left: Mistral M-mark logo + "MISTRAL AI_" wordmark + horizontal link list (Products, Solutions, Research, Blog, Customers, Company).
- Right: "Contact Sales" link + black-pill "Try Studio" CTA.

### Signature Components

**`hero-band-sunset`** — Atmospheric sunset hero band.
- Background gradient `linear-gradient(135deg, {colors.sunshine-700} 0%, {colors.sunshine-900} 60%, {colors.primary} 100%)` overlaid on photographic mountain landscape.
- Layout: hero headline left in `{typography.hero-display}` ({colors.ink}), subtitle in `{typography.subtitle}` ({colors.ink-tint}), button row (`button-dark` + `button-secondary`), atmospheric mountain photography right.

**`sunset-stripe-band`** — Horizontal closing band at the foot of every page.
- Multi-stop gradient: `{colors.primary}` → `{colors.sunshine-700}` → `{colors.sunshine-500}` → `{colors.yellow-saturated}` → `{colors.cream}`.
- Padding `{spacing.lg} 0`. Spans full width, sits above the footer. THIS IS THE BRAND'S MOST RECOGNIZABLE SIGNATURE ELEMENT.

**`cta-banner-cream`** — Page-bottom CTA band on cream surface.
- Background `{colors.cream}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.section}`. "The next chapter of AI is yours." headline in `{typography.heading-1}` (PP Editorial Old), button row below.

**`footer-region`** — Cream-tinted multi-column footer.
- Background `{colors.footer-cream}`, padding `{spacing.section} {spacing.xxl}`.
- 5-column link grid (Why Mistral / Explore / Build / Legal + brand mark column).
- Bottom: language picker + social icons.

**`footer-link`** — Individual footer link.
- Background transparent, text `{colors.primary}`, typography `{typography.body-sm}`, padding `{spacing.xxs} 0`.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Reserve `{colors.primary}` (saturated orange) for primary CTAs and active states only
- Use the **sunset stripe band** at the foot of every page — it's the brand's most recognizable signature
- Pair PP Editorial Old (display) with Inter (UI) — never substitute either with a generic alternative
- Apply `{rounded.md}` (8px) to buttons and `{rounded.lg}` (12px) to cards consistently
- Use cream-yellow surfaces ({colors.cream}) for form panels, feature cards, and footer
- Anchor heroes with photographic mountain-sunset imagery (or its visual equivalent — atmospheric gradient sky)
- Use stat-display token (PP Editorial 56px) for stat callouts to maintain editorial character

### Don't
- Don't use pill-shaped buttons (`{rounded.full}`) — Mistral's geometry is sober and editorial, not playful
- Don't introduce additional accent colors beyond the orange/yellow/cream sunset palette
- Don't reduce hero leading below 1.05 — the editorial display needs that magazine-grade tightness
- Don't replace PP Editorial Old hero displays with Inter — the editorial / sans contrast IS the brand
- Don't apply heavy shadows on flat documentation cards; reserve elevation for IDE mockups
- Don't drop the sunset stripe band from any page bottom — it's the brand's continuity element

## Responsive Behavior

### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile (small) | < 480px | Single column. Hero scales to 40px (PP Editorial). Pill nav collapses to hamburger. Pricing tiers stack 1-up. |
| Mobile (large) | 480 – 767px | Feature tiles 2-up. Hero scales to 52px. |
| Tablet | 768 – 1023px | 2-column feature grids. Pill-tab nav returns. Hero 64px. |
| Desktop | 1024 – 1279px | Multi-column layouts. Hero 76px. Stat row at full width. |
| Wide Desktop | ≥ 1280px | Full 84px hero presentation. |

### Touch Targets
- Buttons render at 40–44px effective height — at WCAG AAA floor with `10px 20px` padding
- Form inputs render at 44px height
- Pill tabs render at ~32px tall — bumps to 44px on mobile

### Collapsing Strategy
- **Promo banner** stays full-width; truncates at < 480px
- **Top nav** below 1024px collapses to hamburger
- **Hero band**: 2-column hero (text + photography) collapses to stacked at < 1024px
- **Pricing tiers**: 4-column desktop → 2-column tablet → 1-column mobile
- **Stat row**: 3-column → stacked at < 768px
- **Hero typography**: 84px → 64px → 52px → 40px
- **Footer**: 5-column desktop → 3-column tablet → 1-column accordion mobile
- **Sunset stripe band** stays full-width on all breakpoints

### Image Behavior
- Mountain-sunset photography uses 16:9 ratio with full-bleed scaling
- IDE mockup images maintain aspect ratio across breakpoints
- Customer logo wall presents wordmarks at consistent 60–80px height

## Iteration Guide

1. Focus on ONE component at a time
2. Reference component names and tokens directly (`{colors.primary}`, `{component-name}-pressed`)
3. Run `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` after edits
4. Add new variants as separate `components:` entries
5. Default to `{typography.body-md}` for body and `{typography.subtitle}` for emphasis. Hero displays use `{typography.hero-display}` (PP Editorial Old).
6. Keep `{colors.primary}` confined to primary CTAs, active states, and the sunset stripe band
7. Cards use `{rounded.lg}` (12px), buttons use `{rounded.md}` (8px). Pills (`{rounded.full}`) reserved for badges only.
8. Always include the sunset-stripe-band component at the foot of every page mockup.

## Known Gaps

- Specific dark-mode token values not surfaced; the brand has not shipped a published dark-mode palette
- Animation/transition timings not extracted; recommend 150–200ms ease for hover/focus state transitions
- Form validation success state not explicitly captured beyond defaults
- Sunset stripe band gradient stops are approximations — the actual values may vary slightly across pages but the visual rhythm is consistent

## Overview

MongoDB carries a strong dual-mode visual identity — dark deep-teal hero bands with the unmistakable bright MongoDB green ({colors.brand-green}) CTA pill paired with stark white documentation and pricing surfaces. The homepage opens with "One data platform. Unlimited AI potential." headline over a deep navy hero, the green pill sitting at the visual center as the primary CTA. Lower on the page, embedded code mockup cards (terminal-aesthetic) sit on the dark hero band, breaking out into white feature cards below. The pricing page renders a 3-tier comparison (Free / Flex / Dedicated) with a featured tier highlighted in soft mint background and bright green border. The MongoDB University page presents a course catalog grid where each tile carries a colored category tag (orange, purple, green, teal) — these are MongoDB's category-encoding accent colors and are the only place outside the brand green where saturated color appears.

The system uses Euclid Circular A as its display face. The face is contemporary geometric — confident but not overly playful — and pairs naturally with both the developer-tool aesthetic of the database product and the educational positioning of the learning surfaces. Cards use `{rounded.lg}` (12px) corners; buttons use `{rounded.full}` pills universally. The brand-teal palette ({colors.brand-teal-deep}) anchors hero bands, footer, code mockups, and the dark CTA banners.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Deep navy/teal hero bands ({colors.brand-teal-deep}) with bright MongoDB green ({colors.brand-green}) CTA pills
- Stark white pricing/documentation surfaces with colored category tags for course tiles (purple, orange, green, teal)
- Euclid Circular A across every UI surface
- Pill-shaped buttons ({rounded.full}) and 12px-rounded cards
- 3-tier pricing comparison (Free / Flex / Dedicated) with featured-mint highlight tier
- Code mockup cards with terminal-aesthetic dark canvas

## Colors

Token coverage was identical across all six pages.

## Typography

### Font Family
**Euclid Circular A** (primary): MongoDB's geometric sans-serif. Fallbacks: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif.
**Source Code Pro** (code): Monospace for code mockups. Fallbacks: 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.hero-display}` | 72px | 500 | 1.10 | -1.5px | Hero ("One data platform") |
| `{typography.display-lg}` | 56px | 500 | 1.15 | -1px | Major section openers |
| `{typography.heading-1}` | 48px | 500 | 1.20 | -0.5px | Page-level headlines |
| `{typography.heading-2}` | 36px | 500 | 1.25 | -0.5px | Subsection headlines |
| `{typography.heading-3}` | 28px | 500 | 1.30 | 0 | Card titles |
| `{typography.heading-4}` | 22px | 500 | 1.35 | 0 | Feature tile titles |
| `{typography.heading-5}` | 18px | 600 | 1.40 | 0 | Smaller card titles, FAQ questions |
| `{typography.subtitle}` | 18px | 400 | 1.50 | 0 | Hero subtitle, lead body |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.55 | 0 | Primary body text |
| `{typography.body-sm}` | 14px | 400 | 1.50 | 0 | Secondary body, table cells |
| `{typography.body-sm-medium}` | 14px | 500 | 1.50 | 0 | Active sidebar, button labels |
| `{typography.caption-bold}` | 13px | 600 | 1.40 | 0 | Badge labels |
| `{typography.micro-uppercase}` | 11px | 600 | 1.40 | 1px | Section eyebrows, course category tags |
| `{typography.button-md}` | 14px | 600 | 1.30 | 0 | Pill button labels |
| `{typography.code-md}` | 14px | 400 | 1.55 | 0 | Code mockups |

### Principles
- Tight hero leading (1.10) on 72px display
- Negative letter-spacing on display sizes (-1.5px to -0.5px)
- 600 weight reserved for buttons and small emphasis (FAQ headings, badges)
- Generous body leading (1.55) for technical documentation readability

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit**: 4px (8px primary increment)
- **Tokens**: `{spacing.xxs}` (4px) through `{spacing.hero}` (120px)
- **Section rhythm**: Marketing pages use `{spacing.section-lg}` (96px); pricing tightens to `{spacing.section}` (64px)

### Grid & Container
- 1280px max-width with 32px gutters
- Pricing: 3-tier card row, dense feature comparison table below
- Learn catalog: 3-up course tile grid, 4-up certification grid
- AI use cases: 2-column hero with atmospheric illustration

### Whitespace Philosophy
Marketing surfaces give content generous breathing room — `{spacing.hero}` (120px) hero padding for deep teal bands. Pricing/learn surfaces tighten dramatically.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (flat) | No shadow; `{colors.hairline}` border | Default cards, table rows |
| 1 (subtle) | `rgba(0, 30, 43, 0.04) 0px 1px 2px 0px` | Hover-elevated tiles |
| 2 (card) | `rgba(0, 30, 43, 0.08) 0px 4px 12px 0px` | Feature cards |
| 3 (mockup) | `rgba(0, 30, 43, 0.12) 0px 12px 24px -4px` | Code mockup over hero |
| 4 (modal) | `rgba(0, 30, 43, 0.16) 0px 16px 48px -8px` | Modals, dropdowns |

### Decorative Depth
- Dark teal hero bands carry atmospheric gradient depth
- Code mockup cards on hero use canvas-dark surface with terminal aesthetic
- Pale-mint pricing-feature tier uses brand-tinted shadow

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.xs}` | 4px | Course category tags |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 6px | Type badges, code chips |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Inputs, search-pill, code blocks |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Cards, pricing tiers, course tiles |
| `{rounded.xl}` | 16px | Larger feature panels |
| `{rounded.xxl}` | 24px | Featured product showcases |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | All buttons, status badges |

### Photography Geometry
- Hero illustrations sit on full-bleed dark backgrounds
- Course tile thumbnails use `{rounded.lg}` corners
- Customer logos wall: wordmarks at consistent 60–80px height

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Use `{colors.brand-green}` (bright MongoDB green) for primary CTAs everywhere
- Pair dark-teal hero bands with bright green CTA pills
- Apply `{rounded.full}` to every button, every status badge
- Apply `{rounded.lg}` (12px) to cards consistently
- Use category accent colors (purple, orange, green, teal) ONLY for course tags
- Maintain Euclid Circular A across every UI surface
- Use code mockup cards with terminal-aesthetic content for product showcases

### Don't
- Don't use the bright green for body text or large surfaces
- Don't introduce additional accent colors beyond the brand green and category-encoding palette
- Don't soften corners on buttons; the pill is a brand signature
- Don't replace deep teal hero bands with white hero bands
- Don't apply heavy shadows on flat documentation cards; reserve elevation for code mockups
- Don't use Source Code Pro for prose

## Responsive Behavior

### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile (small) | < 480px | Single column. Hero 36px. Pricing 1-up. Course catalog 1-up. |
| Mobile (large) | 480 – 767px | Course tiles 2-up. Hero 48px. |
| Tablet | 768 – 1023px | 2-column feature grids. Hero 56px. |
| Desktop | 1024 – 1279px | 3-tier pricing card row. 3-up course catalog. Hero 64px. |
| Wide Desktop | ≥ 1280px | Full 72px hero presentation. |

### Touch Targets
- Pill buttons render at 40–44px effective height
- Form inputs render at 44px height
- Search pill (large) renders at 56px
- Pill tabs ~32px → 44px on mobile

### Collapsing Strategy
- **Promo banner** stays full-width; truncates at < 480px
- **Top nav** below 1024px collapses to hamburger
- **Hero band**: code mockup card moves below text on mobile
- **Pricing tiers**: 3-column → 2-column tablet → 1-column mobile
- **Course catalog**: 3-up → 2-up tablet → 1-up mobile
- **Hero typography**: 72px → 56px → 48px → 36px
- **Footer**: 6-column desktop → 3-column tablet → accordion mobile

### Image Behavior
- Atmospheric AI imagery uses 16:9 ratio with full-bleed scaling
- Code mockup card content remains readable across breakpoints
- Customer logo wall: wordmarks at consistent 60–80px height

## Iteration Guide

1. Focus on ONE component at a time
2. Reference component names and tokens directly
3. Run `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` after edits
4. Add new variants as separate `components:` entries
5. Default to `{typography.body-md}` for body
6. Keep `{colors.brand-green}` as the primary CTA across all surfaces
7. Pill-shaped buttons (`{rounded.full}`) always
8. Dark-teal hero bands frame primary CTAs

## Known Gaps

- Specific dark-mode token values for canvas/surface beyond hero bands not surfaced
- Animation/transition timings not extracted; recommend 150–200ms ease
- Form validation success state not explicitly captured
- Course-tile category color mappings are observation-based

    backgroundColor: "{colors.surface}"
    rounded: "{rounded.md}"
    padding: "{spacing.sm} {spacing.md}"
    typography: "{typography.body}"

---


## Overview

mydealz is a deals-community feed running at maximum density: a single cool-gray canvas (`{colors.canvas}`) stacked with hundreds of white deal cards (`{colors.surface}`), each one a compact bundle of thumbnail, title, price, and social signals. The design's whole job is to make that firehose scannable, and it does it with one confident brand green (`{colors.primary}`) — the color of every price, every "Zum Deal" pill, every submit action — plus a tight status vocabulary that keeps the eye moving.

The signature move is the **temperature control**: every deal carries a pill showing a cold-blue down-arrow (`{colors.cold}`), the deal's crowd-voted temperature in hot-red (`{colors.hot}`), and a hot-red up-arrow — pricing turned into a live vote. That red/blue pairing, extended by a warm orange (`{colors.warm}`) for rising deals and a premium violet (`{colors.premium}`) for highlighted content, is the brand's playful counterweight to an otherwise businesslike grid. Discount percentages sit in soft mint pills (`{colors.discount-surface}`), so a card reads at a glance: green price, red-hot temperature, mint saving.

Geometrically the system is defined by the **fully-round 540px pill** — buttons, the search field, the temperature control, filter chips all curve to a complete radius, while content cards settle at a friendly 8px. Averta CY carries everything at just two weights (medium 500, bold 700), keeping headlines punchy and the dense body legible. Depth is minimal: cards separate with a hairline (`{colors.hairline}`) and lift on the softest shadow only when they matter.

**Key Characteristics:**
- One brand green (`{colors.primary}`) owns every action and every price — the single unifying signal across a chaotic feed
- Signature hot/cold **temperature control**: `{colors.cold}` down-vote, `{colors.hot}` up-vote and temperature reading, on every deal card
- Fully-round `{rounded.full}` (540px) pills for buttons, search, chips, and the temperature control; 8px cards
- Mint discount pills (`{colors.discount-surface}`) pairing green savings against the red-hot temperature
- Averta CY at two weights (500/700) driving a punchy, high-density type system
- Cool-gray canvas (`{colors.canvas}`) behind stacked white cards (`{colors.surface}`) — a scannable card feed, not a marketing page
- A compact accent set — `{colors.warm}` orange for rising, `{colors.premium}` violet for highlighted — kept strictly functional

## Colors

### Brand & Accent
- **Deal Green** (`{colors.primary}` — #30a83c): The brand's core. Fills every primary CTA pill, every deal price, submit actions, active links, and highlighted stats. On-color content is `{colors.on-primary}`.
- **Strong Green** (`{colors.green-strong}`): A darker green for green text on light surfaces (discount-badge label, outline-button glyphs) where the fill green would be too light.
- **Hot Red** (`{colors.hot}`): The temperature "hot" signal — the deal's degree reading and the up-vote arrow. The brand's excitement color.
- **Cold Blue** (`{colors.cold}`): The temperature "cold" signal — the down-vote arrow. Always paired against `{colors.hot}` in the temperature control.
- **Rising Orange** (`{colors.warm}`): A warm accent for rising/trending deals, sitting between cold and hot on the temperature spectrum.
- **Premium Violet** (`{colors.premium}`): Highlight accent for premium / featured content markers.
- **Discount Mint** (`{colors.discount-surface}`): The soft green pill behind a saving percentage.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}`): The cool light-gray page ground that stacked white cards sit on.
- **Surface** (`{colors.surface}`): Pure white — every card, the nav, the footer, buttons.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}`): The 1px border on cards, buttons, and dividers.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}`): True black for deal titles, headings, and primary text.
- **Body** (`{colors.body}`): Mid gray for secondary copy, metadata, muted button labels.
- **Muted** (`{colors.muted}`): Light gray for the quietest captions and placeholder text.

### Semantic
- **Warning Surface / Text** (`{colors.warning-surface}` / `{colors.warning-text}`): The soft-yellow pill and amber-brown text used for expiring / caution deal states.

## Typography

### Font Family

**Averta CY** — a humanist geometric sans — carries the entire system at two weights: medium (500) for body and lead copy, bold (700) for headings, UI labels, prices, and micro-labels. A **monospace** face appears in rare technical contexts (voucher codes). There is no light or black weight; the two-weight discipline keeps the dense feed consistent.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display}` | 48px | 700 | 1.1 | 0 | Page hero headline |
| `{typography.heading-lg}` | 24px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Section titles, deal price |
| `{typography.heading}` | 20px | 700 | 1.25 | 0 | Card / block headings |
| `{typography.lead}` | 18px | 500 | 1.4 | 0 | Lead paragraphs, prominent links |
| `{typography.body}` | 16px | 500 | 1.5 | 0 | Body copy, deal descriptions |
| `{typography.ui}` | 14px | 700 | 1.3 | 0 | Button labels, temperature, badges |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 500 | 1.3 | 0 | Metadata, timestamps |
| `{typography.micro}` | 10px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Micro-labels, counts |
| `{typography.mono}` | 16px | 500 | 1.4 | 0 | Voucher codes |

### Principles
- Two weights only — 500 for reading, 700 for everything that signals or acts.
- Prices and temperatures are always bold; they're the two numbers that matter most on a card.
- The dense feed leans on size and weight, never on color, for text hierarchy (color is reserved for status).

### Note on Font Substitutes
Averta CY is a commercial face. For open-source builds, **Mulish** or **Nunito Sans** (500/700) reproduce the humanist-geometric warmth with near-identical metrics; keep the two-weight split. Any system monospace substitutes for the voucher-code face.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit**: 8px
- **Tokens (front matter)**: `{spacing.xxs}` 2px · `{spacing.xs}` 4px · `{spacing.sm}` 8px · `{spacing.md}` 12px · `{spacing.lg}` 16px · `{spacing.xl}` 24px · `{spacing.xxl}` 40px
- Cards pad `{spacing.lg}`; card rows stack with `{spacing.sm}`–`{spacing.md}` gaps for maximum density.

### Grid & Container
A two-column shell above ~768px: the main deal feed (single stacked column of full-width cards) plus a right sidebar of coupon, news, and discussion cards. Below the breakpoint the sidebar drops and the feed goes full-width. The container is wide and content-dense rather than a narrow reading column.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Whitespace is rationed — this is an information product, not a marketing page. Cards sit close together with tight internal padding; the cool-gray canvas gutters between white cards do the separating work, and the hairline borders keep each card crisp against its neighbors.

### Responsive Strategy

#### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | < 768px | Single-column feed; sidebar drops; nav collapses to the "Menü" pill; temperature control and CTA stack under the card body |
| Desktop | ≥ 768px | Feed + right sidebar two-column shell; full nav row with search pill and category strip |

#### Touch Targets
Pill buttons (`{components.button-primary}`) and the temperature control clear a comfortable tap height; vote arrows, comment, share, and bookmark icons carry generous hit areas on the card foot.

#### Collapsing Strategy
The category strip and right sidebar collapse first; the nav condenses to the "Menü" pill + search + submit; deal cards reflow from a media-left row into a stacked thumbnail-over-body layout on narrow screens.

#### Image Behavior
Deal thumbnails are contained in `{rounded.md}` frames on the card's media side, never full-bleed; avatars are perfect circles (`{rounded.circle}`). Merchant logos and app-store badges render inline at fixed heights.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Flat on `{colors.canvas}` | Page ground, footer |
| 1 | 1px `{colors.hairline}` border | Deal cards, sidebar cards, buttons, inputs |
| 2 | Soft shadow `rgba(11,22,44,0.09) 0 4px 12px` | Elevated / hovered cards, dropdowns |
| 3 | Deeper drop `rgba(0,0,0,0.38) -1px 11px 15px -11px` | Overlays, sticky bars |

Depth is hairline-first. Cards separate by border and canvas gutter; the soft 4–12px shadow is reserved for elements that lift (menus, sticky bars, elevated cards). There are no heavy shadow stacks in the resting feed.

### Decorative Depth
The brand's playfulness lives in illustration, not gradients — a green cartoon frog mascot and companion characters appear in the consent and empty-state surfaces. The palette itself is flat; there are no brand gradients.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.xs}` | 2px | Tightest inline chips |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Discount / filled badges, small tags |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Deal cards, sidebar cards, thumbnails, tag buttons |
| `{rounded.full}` | 540px | Buttons, search pill, temperature control, filter chips — the pill signature |
| `{rounded.circle}` | 9999px | Avatars, icon buttons |

### Photography Geometry
Deal thumbnails sit in `{rounded.md}` frames on the card's media column; author and community avatars are circles (`{rounded.circle}`). There is no hero photography — the product IS the card grid.

## Components

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — the green action ("Zum Deal", "Deal-Alarm anlegen", "Hinzufügen")
- Fill `{colors.primary}`, label `{colors.on-primary}` in `{typography.ui}`, shape `{rounded.full}`, padding `0px 14px`, often with a trailing external-link or plus glyph

**`button-outline-green`** — brand-tinted secondary ("+ Beitrag")
- `{colors.surface}` fill, `{colors.primary}` label + border, `{rounded.full}`, padding `0px 14px`

**`button-outline-neutral`** — quiet chrome ("Menü")
- `{colors.surface}` fill, `{colors.ink}` label, `{colors.hairline}` border, `{rounded.full}`, padding `0px 12px`

**`button-muted`** — de-emphasized action ("Ohne Zustimmung weiter")
- `{colors.surface}` fill, `{colors.body}` label, `{colors.hairline}` border, `{rounded.full}`

**`button-tag`** — compact utility control
- `{colors.surface}` fill, `{colors.ink}` label, `{rounded.md}`, tight `0px 4px` padding

### Cards & Containers

**`deal-card`** — the feed's atom
- `{colors.surface}` on `{colors.hairline}`, `{rounded.md}`, `{spacing.lg}` padding; media-left thumbnail, bold black title, a `price-lockup`, a `temperature-control`, merchant + author line, and a `button-primary` foot with comment/share/bookmark icons

**`sidebar-card`** — coupon / news / discussion tiles
- Same white-on-hairline `{rounded.md}` chrome as `deal-card`, in the right rail

**`timestamp-pill`** — "Gepostet vor …" marker
- `{colors.canvas}` fill, `{colors.body}` `{typography.caption}`, `{rounded.md}`, pinned top-right on a card

### Inputs & Forms

**`search-pill`** — the header search
- `{colors.surface}` pill at `{rounded.full}`, `{colors.hairline}` border, `{colors.body}` placeholder in `{typography.body}`, magnifier glyph left

**`text-input`**
- `{colors.surface}` field, `{colors.ink}` text, navy-translucent border, fully-round `{rounded.full}`, padding `9px 35px`

**`email-input`**
- `{colors.surface}` field at `{rounded.md}` (square-cornered against the pill search), padding `9px 16px`

### Navigation

**`nav-bar`**
- `{colors.surface}` bar with `{colors.hairline}` bottom rule: mydealz frog logo, `button-outline-neutral` "Menü", `search-pill`, "Deal-Alarm anlegen" and "Einloggen" text links, `button-outline-green` "+ Beitrag"; a category strip (Kategorien, Gutscheine, Freebies, Deals, Diskussionen, Club) sits below

**`footer`**
- `{colors.surface}` over a `{colors.hairline}` top rule; link columns (Firma, Community, Rechtliches) in `{colors.body}` with green links, social circle icons, app-store badges, and a `country-selector`

**`country-selector`**
- `{colors.surface}` `{rounded.md}` dropdown with flag + label, `{colors.hairline}` border

### Signature Components

**`temperature-control`** — the brand's defining component
- A fully-round `{rounded.full}` pill: `temperature-down` cold-blue (`{colors.cold}`) down-arrow, the deal's temperature reading in hot-red (`{colors.hot}`), and a `temperature-up` hot-red up-arrow — the crowd's price vote made visible

**`temperature-up`** / **`temperature-down`** — the vote arrows
- Up in `{colors.hot}`, down in `{colors.cold}`, both in `{typography.ui}`

**`price-lockup`** — the deal's number
- `{colors.primary}` green current price in `{typography.heading-lg}`, a struck-through `{colors.muted}` original, and a `discount-badge`

**`discount-badge`** — the saving
- `{colors.discount-surface}` mint pill with `{colors.green-strong}` label in `{typography.ui}`, `{rounded.sm}`, `4px 8px`

**`badge-neutral-subtle`** / **`badge-filled`** — status chips
- Subtle: white / black / `{rounded.md}`. Filled: `{colors.canvas}` fill, `{colors.body}` text, `{rounded.sm}` with a white hairline

**`premium-badge`** — highlighted-content marker
- `{colors.premium}` violet label on `{colors.surface}`, `{rounded.sm}`

**`warning-badge`** — expiring / caution state
- `{colors.warning-surface}` soft-yellow pill, `{colors.warning-text}` amber-brown label, `{rounded.sm}`

**`avatar`** — author / community
- Circle (`{rounded.circle}`) on `{colors.canvas}` with a white ring

### Examples (illustrative)

> Kit-mirror demonstration surfaces. These are not brand-native components — each `ex-*` entry references the brand primitives above so every example surface is shaped by this spec rather than template defaults.

**`ex-pricing-tier`** — Default Pricing tier card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with brand canvas-soft surface.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `borderColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-pricing-tier-featured`** — Featured/highlighted tier — polarity-flipped surface (dark fill + light text in light mode, light fill + dark text in dark mode).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-product-selector`** — What's Included summary card — re-purposed for SaaS / B2B verticals (NOT a literal product gallery).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-cart-drawer`** — Subscription summary — re-purposed for SaaS / B2B (line items per add-on, not literal cart).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `item-divider`

**`ex-app-shell-row`** — Sidebar nav row inside the App Shell example. Active state uses brand primary as the indicator.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `activeIndicator`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-data-table-cell`** — Default data-table th + td chrome. Header uses mono-caps eyebrow typography; body uses body-sm.
- Properties: `headerBackground`, `headerTypography`, `bodyTypography`, `cellPadding`, `rowBorder`

**`ex-auth-form-card`** — Sign-in / sign-up card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with text-input primitives inside.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-modal-card`** — Modal dialog surface — same chrome as feature-card with elevated shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-empty-state-card`** — Empty-state illustration frame.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `captionTypography`

**`ex-toast`** — Toast notification surface — feature-card shape + medium shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `typography`


## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Reserve `{colors.primary}` green for actions and prices — it is the single thread tying the feed together.
- Keep the `temperature-control` pairing intact: `{colors.cold}` down, `{colors.hot}` up and temperature — it's the brand's signature.
- Pill every button, chip, search, and the temperature control to `{rounded.full}`; keep content cards at `{rounded.md}`.
- Put savings in the `{colors.discount-surface}` mint badge beside the green price.
- Hold typography to Averta CY 500 / 700; bold every price and temperature.
- Separate cards with `{colors.hairline}` borders and the `{colors.canvas}` gutter, not heavy shadows.

### Don't
- Don't recolor prices or primary actions away from `{colors.primary}` green.
- Don't split the temperature pairing or recolor the vote arrows — cold is blue, hot is red, always.
- Don't introduce shadows on resting feed cards; the soft 4–12px shadow is for elements that lift.
- Don't use a third or fourth type weight — the system is 500 and 700 only.
- Don't let `{colors.warm}` orange or `{colors.premium}` violet drift into decorative use; they are functional status colors.
- Don't square off the pills — the fully-round `{rounded.full}` button is the brand's shape signature.

## Overview

NerdWallet is a comparison engine wearing an editorial coat, and the design reflects both halves. Article pages open on a wide `{colors.primary}` gradient band carrying a white headline, a byline row and a set of trust badges — the only place the brand raises its voice. Everything below that band drops to `{colors.canvas}` and `{colors.canvas-soft}`, where dense rate tables and product cards do the actual work. The transition is abrupt by design: one saturated green rectangle, then a very long, very quiet document.

The palette is almost monochromatic in hue. `{colors.primary}` is a deep spruce green that fills every button, every active tab and every rating star, and beneath it sits a full ladder of mints — `{colors.mint-50}`, `{colors.mint-100}`, `{colors.mint-200}` — that wash section panels, icon tiles and photo frames. Those mints carry enormous surface area, far more than any accent, which is what keeps a page of financial tables from reading as a spreadsheet. The only colours outside the green family are `{colors.link}` for inline links and a lime family used for emphasis.

The shape language is the surprise. For a consumer product this heavily illustrated, the corners are nearly square: the primary button sits at `{rounded.xs}` — two pixels — and cards rarely exceed `{rounded.lg}`. There is essentially no elevation; the single shadow in the system is a very wide, very faint double-layer stack. Separation is done with `{colors.hairline}` rules and mint fills instead. The result reads as trustworthy and utilitarian rather than soft.

**Key Characteristics:**
- One deep green, `{colors.primary}`, fills every action and every active state across all page types.
- A three-step mint ladder (`{colors.mint-50}` → `{colors.mint-100}` → `{colors.mint-200}`) carries the largest surfaces in the system.
- Buttons are nearly square at `{rounded.xs}`; the shape language stays tight even where illustration is playful.
- Almost shadowless — `{colors.hairline}` rules and mint washes replace elevation.
- Editorial pages follow a fixed rhythm: green gradient band → white body → mint callout → white comparison table.
- A lime family (`{colors.lime-hero}`, `{colors.lime-panel}`, `{colors.lime-accent}`) supplies emphasis that green cannot, since green is spent on controls.
- Headings sit in pure `{colors.ink}` black, not a softened near-black.

## Colors

Source pages: the homepage, the high-yield savings comparison page, and the best-credit-cards page.

### Brand & Accent

- **Spruce** (`{colors.primary}` — #008254): the brand. It fills `{button-primary}`, `{icon-circle-active}`, rating stars and every in-body green link, and it is the base of the editorial hero gradient. By pixel volume it is the single most-used non-neutral in the system.
- **Deep Spruce** (`{colors.primary-deep}` — #006642): the fill of `{stat-block-dark}`, the dark statistic panel that sits inside the mint expert-tip callout.
- **Forest** (`{colors.forest}` — #00482f): the deepest green, used where the hero gradient lands darkest and on dense editorial chrome.
- **Logo Lime** (`{colors.logo-lime}` — #8dc63f): the lime inside the wordmark's leading mark. It appears at small scale on every page and nowhere else.
- **Hero Lime** (`{colors.lime-hero}` — #9ae600): the vivid lime that sets the brand name inside the homepage hero headline — one word, once per page.
- **Panel Lime** (`{colors.lime-panel}` — #e8fdac): the fill of `{expert-tip-panel}` and the colour of `{editorial-badge}` text on the green band.
- **Accent Lime** (`{colors.lime-accent}` — #ddfa88): a brighter lime used for highlight marks on the comparison pages.
- **Ribbon Lime** (`{colors.lime-ribbon}` — #a8ea4c): the lime end of the `{marquee-ribbon}` gradient — the only place the lime family covers a large surface.

### Surface

- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #ffffff): the page, the nav bar and every card.
- **Soft Canvas** (`{colors.canvas-soft}` — #f7f7f7): the page tint behind long comparison pages and the fill of `{button-secondary}`. It carries more area than any other surface on the savings page.
- **Mint 50** (`{colors.mint-50}` — #effcf8): the palest wash, used for `{section-panel-mint}` and `{icon-circle-inactive}`.
- **Mint 100** (`{colors.mint-100}` — #e3faf2): one step up, used for `{media-frame-mint}` and `{award-ribbon-pill}`.
- **Mint 200** (`{colors.mint-200}` — #b7ecda): the most saturated mint, reserved for small emphasis fills.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #ebebec): rules between table rows and inside cards.
- **Strong Hairline** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — #d8d9da): the visible border on `{product-card}` and `{button-outline}`.

### Text

- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #000000): every heading and product name. Pure black, not softened.
- **Body** (`{colors.body}` — #3d4045): running copy and `{spec-cell}` labels.
- **Muted** (`{colors.muted}` — #64666a): captions, disclosure lines and `{eyebrow-label}`.
- **Faint** (`{colors.faint}` — #b1b3b5): the quietest tier, used for de-emphasised metadata.

### Semantic

- **Link** (`{colors.link}` — #005fb9): inline links inside tables and cards, always underlined.
- **Info** (`{colors.info}` — #4b99e6): a lighter blue used for supporting informational marks.
- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — #de2828): the system's validation and destructive red, reserved for form errors and removal actions.

## Typography

### Font Family

**Gotham** and **GothamDisplay** carry the entire system. Gotham handles body copy, UI labels, captions and the largest homepage headline; GothamDisplay — the tighter-fitting display cut — takes most editorial headings between 14 and 40px. The pairing is unusual in that the display cut is used at *smaller* sizes than the text cut's maximum, so the two overlap through the middle of the scale rather than splitting cleanly at a size boundary.

The weight range is wide and genuinely used: 300 for body copy, 500 and 600 for interface text, 700 for headings and labels, and 900 available at the top. Body copy at weight 300 against 700 headings is what gives the long editorial pages their airy feel despite very tight corner radii. A serif, **Chronicle Display**, appears on the long-form editorial pages as a secondary face.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-xl}` | 52px | 700 | 1.15 | 0 | Homepage hero headline |
| `{typography.display-lg}` | 40px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Editorial page headline |
| `{typography.heading-1}` | 36px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Section headline |
| `{typography.heading-2}` | 28px | 700 | 1.25 | 0 | Sub-section headline |
| `{typography.stat-value}` | 24px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Statistic figure |
| `{typography.heading-3}` | 20px | 700 | 1.3 | 0 | Card title |
| `{typography.heading-4}` | 20px | 500 | 1.3 | 0 | Light sub-heading |
| `{typography.body-lg}` | 18px | 300 | 1.5 | 0 | Lead paragraph |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 300 | 1.5 | 0 | Body copy |
| `{typography.body-sm}` | 14px | 300 | 1.5 | 0 | Table copy, captions |
| `{typography.ui-label}` | 14px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Button and nav labels |
| `{typography.ui-sm}` | 13px | 500 | 1.3 | 0 | Dense interface text |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 500 | 1.4 | 0 | Field labels, disclosures |
| `{typography.eyebrow}` | 12px | 700 | 1.2 | 0 | Uppercase section labels |
| `{typography.micro}` | 11px | 500 | 1.4 | 0 | Trust badges, fine print |

### Principles

Hierarchy is carried by weight contrast more than by size. The gap between weight-300 body and weight-700 headings is wide enough that adjacent sizes (20px heading against 18px lead) still read as distinct levels. Uppercase is reserved for two roles — `{typography.eyebrow}` section labels and button text — and never used for headings.

### Note on Font Substitutes

Gotham and GothamDisplay are licensed faces. **Montserrat** is the closest widely-available geometric substitute for Gotham, though it runs slightly wider and needs a small negative tracking at display sizes; **Proxima Nova** or **Jost** are nearer in proportion if available. Keep the 300 weight for body copy — dropping to 400 collapses the weight contrast the hierarchy depends on. Substitute the editorial serif with **Playfair Display** or **Source Serif 4**.

## Layout

### Spacing System

- **Base unit**: 8px.
- **Tokens**: `{spacing.xxs}` 4px · `{spacing.xs}` 8px · `{spacing.sm}` 12px · `{spacing.md}` 16px · `{spacing.lg}` 20px · `{spacing.xl}` 24px · `{spacing.xxl}` 32px · `{spacing.section}` 40px.
- `{spacing.md}` is the universal control padding — both `{button-primary}` and `{button-secondary}` use a flat 16px on all sides, which is what gives the buttons their square, chunky proportion.
- `{button-outline}` breaks that pattern with `8px 16px`, making it visibly shorter than the filled buttons beside it.

### Grid & Container

Content centres in a container of roughly 1200px inside the 1280px viewport. The homepage runs a 5-up category tile grid that steps down to 4-up and 2-up. Editorial pages use a single wide column for the hero band and then a full-width comparison table with five semantic columns — institution, rating, headline rate, bonus, and action. Product cards on the credit-cards page are full-width blocks stacked vertically, each subdivided into a spec grid of three to four cells.

### Whitespace Philosophy

Whitespace is tight inside components and generous between them. Table rows sit close together with only a hairline separating them, but the gap between one comparison block and the next is large. The mint panels act as breathing room that still carries content — rather than leaving empty space, the system drops in a pale `{colors.mint-50}` band and lets the density fall instead.

### Responsive Strategy

#### Breakpoints

| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Small mobile | < 425px | Single column; comparison tables become stacked cards; nav reduces to logo plus menu |
| Mobile | 425–599px | Single column; spec grids collapse to one-per-row |
| Large mobile | 600–767px | Two-up category tiles; table columns begin to drop |
| Tablet | 768–1023px | Category rail scrolls horizontally; product cards keep their action column |
| Laptop | 1024–1279px | Full table layout with tightened gutters |
| Desktop | ≥ 1280px | Full layout at container width |

#### Touch Targets

`{button-primary}` and `{button-secondary}` clear 44×44 comfortably at their flat `{spacing.md}` padding. `{button-outline}` at `8px 16px` sits close to the minimum and needs its hit area extended on touch widths. `{icon-circle-active}` and `{icon-circle-inactive}` render near 44px in the category rail.

#### Collapsing Strategy

The nav keeps the wordmark, search and both account controls as long as possible, dropping the category links first. The horizontal category rail on comparison pages becomes a scrolling strip rather than wrapping. Comparison tables are the main responsive event: below the tablet breakpoint each row reflows into a stacked card where the institution logo, rating and rate become vertical fields and the action button goes full-width. `{expert-tip-panel}` keeps its mint fill but drops `{stat-block-dark}` beneath the copy instead of beside it.

#### Image Behavior

Institution logos are supplied as fixed-height greyscale-friendly marks and never crop. Editorial illustration sits inside `{media-frame-mint}` at `{rounded.xxxl}`. Product art — credit-card faces — renders at a fixed small aspect inside `{product-card}` and is never full-bleed. Author avatars are circular at `{rounded.full}` in a small overlapping stack.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Flat on `{colors.canvas}` | Body copy, table rows, headings |
| 1 | 1px `{colors.hairline}` rule | Row dividers, spec-cell separators |
| 2 | 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border | `{product-card}`, `{button-outline}`, `{accordion-row}` |
| 3 | `rgba(100,102,106,0.05) 0 4px 16px` plus `rgba(100,102,104,0.05) 0 16px 40px` | `{button-primary}` and the few floating surfaces |
| 4 | `oklab(0 0 0 / 0.04) 0 20px 25px -5px` plus `0 8px 10px -6px` | Overlay surfaces |

The system is deliberately flat. Both shadow definitions sit at 4–5% opacity and spread very wide, so they register as a faint settling rather than a lift. On a page of financial data this reads as precision: nothing floats, everything is ruled.

### Decorative Depth

Depth comes from colour blocking and illustration, not from shadow. The green hero band is the only saturated plane; beneath it the mint ladder creates shallow steps between sections. Illustration is flat-vector — coin stacks, piggy banks, houses — sitting directly on white or mint with no drop shadow. The one genuinely dimensional element is the arrow motif inside `{stat-block-dark}`, which reads as a chart line breaking out of its container.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | `{text-input}`, `{award-ribbon-pill}`, table edges |
| `{rounded.xxs}` | 1px | Inline marks |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 2px | `{button-primary}`, `{button-secondary}`, search field |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Small containers and inline blocks |
| `{rounded.md}` | 6px | App-store badges |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 8px | `{product-card}`, `{button-outline}`, `{accordion-row}`, `{expert-tip-panel}`, `{stat-block-dark}` |
| `{rounded.xl}` | 10px | Labels and small spans |
| `{rounded.xxl}` | 12px | `{category-tile}` |
| `{rounded.xxxl}` | 16px | `{section-panel-mint}`, `{media-frame-mint}` |
| `{rounded.tooltip}` | 20px | Tooltip surfaces |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Avatars, `{icon-circle-active}`, `{icon-circle-inactive}` |

The scale is broad but the weight of usage sits at the small end. Controls live at `{rounded.xs}`, cards at `{rounded.lg}`, and only decorative surfaces — mint panels and photo frames — reach `{rounded.xxxl}`. Several components use asymmetric radii, rounding only their top or leading corners where they butt against an adjacent block.

### Photography Geometry

Editorial photography sits inside `{media-frame-mint}` at `{rounded.xxxl}`, typically at a portrait or square crop. Author avatars are `{rounded.full}` at roughly 32px, overlapped in threes. Institution logos are placed on white at their native aspect with generous padding so competing brand marks never touch. Illustration is used at roughly 64px square inside `{category-tile}`.

## Components

> Every spec below documents Default and, where extracted, Active states only.

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — the green action ("SIGN UP", "APPLY NOW", "LEARN MORE")
- Background `{colors.primary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.ui-label}`, rounded `{rounded.xs}`, padding `{spacing.md}`, Elevation Level 3.
- Uppercase label. The flat 16px padding on all four sides is what gives it its blocky proportion, and the 2px radius keeps it reading as a rectangle rather than a pill.

**`button-secondary`** — the quiet companion ("SIGN IN")
- Background `{colors.canvas-soft}`, text `{colors.primary}`, type `{typography.ui-label}`, rounded `{rounded.xs}`, padding `{spacing.md}`.
- Same geometry as `{button-primary}` with the fill and text roles swapped, so the pair reads as one control with two weights.

**`button-outline`** — the compact utility control
- Text `{colors.primary}`, type `{typography.ui-label}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `8px 16px`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, no fill.
- The only button that departs from both the square radius and the flat padding — noticeably shorter and softer than the filled pair.

- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-md}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, Elevation Level 2.
- The workhorse of the comparison pages: product name, star rating, a `{button-primary}` action column on the right, then a spec grid of `{spec-cell}` blocks and a stack of `{accordion-row}` disclosures.

- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-sm}`, rounded `{rounded.xxl}`.

**`section-panel-mint`**
- Background `{colors.mint-50}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.xxxl}`.

- Background `{colors.mint-100}`, rounded `{rounded.xxxl}`. Holds editorial photography with the mint visible as a border-like margin around the image.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Spend `{colors.primary}` on actions and active states only — buttons, rating stars, active tabs, in-body links.
- Reach for the mint ladder (`{colors.mint-50}` → `{colors.mint-200}`) when a section needs separation; it is the system's substitute for elevation.
- Keep controls at `{rounded.xs}` and cards at `{rounded.lg}`; save `{rounded.xxxl}` for decorative panels and photo frames.
- Separate table rows with a single `{colors.hairline}` rule and no vertical dividers.
- Use the lime family for emphasis that has to survive on a green ground, where `{colors.primary}` would disappear.
- Set headings in `{colors.ink}` pure black and body copy at weight 300 — the weight gap is the hierarchy.
- Give every comparison figure a `{typography.caption}` label above it in `{colors.body}`, never inline.
- Open editorial pages with `{hero-band}` and then drop immediately to a light canvas; do not carry the green further down.

### Don't

- Don't round the filled buttons. `{rounded.xs}` is a deliberate choice against the softness of the illustration style.
- Don't add drop shadows to cards — use the `{colors.hairline-strong}` border instead. The system's only shadows sit at 4–5% opacity.
- Don't use `{colors.link}` blue and `{colors.primary}` green interchangeably; blue is a supporting reference, green is navigation the reader is meant to follow.
- Don't extend `{hero-band}` green into body sections or use it as a card fill.
- Don't introduce a warm accent. The palette runs green through mint with blue as the only outside hue.
- Don't set body copy above weight 300 or headings below 700 — collapsing the gap flattens the hierarchy.
- Don't place `{colors.lime-panel}` on white as a text colour; the lime tier only works as a fill on white or as type on green.
- Don't give `{text-input}` a radius or a border of its own; the containing chrome supplies both.
